note: Generated from E:/theory by tools/export.mjs. Do not edit; edit the yaml and re-export. Numbers tagged design are starting values, not doctrine.

rules.task: Decide what shape a bot's force should have at this size
rules.when: A bot buys or re-plans, and its squads on hand are known
do: Up to 6 squads: one base of fire and one maneuver element, keeping a squad back at first if there are enough. Don't split further.
7 to 15: support group, two maneuver groups, a small reserve.
16 to 28: support group, company-size groups, a real reserve.
Change shape at a phase change, never during an assault.

rules.task: Decide which roles must exist before others grow
rules.when: Choosing the next purchases
do: Have a base of fire (mg) before adding more maneuver squads.
Have anti-tank means before the enemy can field armor, and more once it does.
Buy tanks with supporting infantry and fire, not as a tank-only force.
A tank alone doesn't count as a group: keep tanks in twos or more.

flavor.ger_reported: tank commander leads the combat team, all arms under him

pitfalls: Don't apply MP or CP price sheets; prices belong to the mod.

rules.task: Decide how to respond to seen enemy armor in the buy
rules.when: Enemy armor is seen, or could arrive and its strength is unknown
do: Strength unknown: hold anti-tank means massed, in one place you can move.
Small-scale armor only: spread light anti-tank among forward groups.
Fewer anti-tank weapons on hand means a larger share massed.

scale.share: role share of force at each shape

rules.task: Decide how much force and income to keep unspent
rules.when: Any purchase or commitment while a fight is on
do: Treat unspent income as part of the reserve: keep enough for one group's worth of answers (design).
Spend it at once for a decisive blow, a counterattack, or to restart a stalled attack.
After spending, rebuild a reserve from relieved units before attacking again.

scale.amount: one group at the current shape

rules.task: Choose where a team or bot attacks
rules.when: Team or bot is choosing where to attack
do: Score axes by cover on the way in and by enemy strength; pick one.
Team: one bot or pair is main effort, the others hold or fix.
Bot: most maneuver groups on that axis; the rest press to split the enemy.
If a unit isn't stopped, it keeps going while neighbors are halted.

flavor.uk: press through gaps, regardless of earlier objective
flavor.su: leaders push through gaps on own initiative, even off direction
flavor.jp_reported: attacks even on thin artillery preparation: a known risk

pitfalls: Stock bot Lua orders only Spawn, CaptureFlag and SayChat (MIS-08).

rules.task: Set how wide a group spreads
rules.when: Assigning a group a width on the map
do: Attack width W: 1.0 x mg per company-shape bot, 0.5 x mg per platoon-shape bot (design).
Defense width 2 x W, delay width 4 x W. A bot only fixing or holding uses 2 x W.
Widen by gaps between groups covered by fire, not by thinning a group.
Too narrow also fails: bunching raises losses.

scale.W: scale with group size and profile mg range

rules.task: Order a group forward once in contact
rules.when: Group in contact, or moving where the enemy can fire
do: Split: base of fire pins, maneuver moves. They may swap.
Site the base to fire obliquely, about 0.6 to 0.8 x mg from the objective (design).
Maneuver goes by a covered route that isn't the obvious one, never a wide loop in the open.
Keep on the first post; detach the least possible to answer flank fire.

flavor.uk: fire section plus flanking sections, drilled
flavor.su: more open ground means shorter, faster rushes
flavor.jp_reported: final deployment in time to fire over the last stretch
flavor.us: long bounds only under overwhelming fire

pitfalls: No suppression model in stock AS2 and morale follows health: pinning is really hurting.

rules.task: Time an assault and its supporting fire
rules.when: Maneuver group is near the objective
do: Close to the nearest point that doesn't mask supporting fire, then assault.
Before that, move guns toward the flank of the resistance, so they fire longest.
When masked, mg and mortars shift to enemy beside or behind the objective.
Assault together. A piecemeal assault loses much of its effect.

rules.task: Decide when to commit the reserve
rules.when: A group is held back, or an attack stalls
do: Exposed flank or unclear enemy: hold back more, up to two of three groups.
Hold while fires or other groups can restart the attack.
Commit whole, at once, at a flank or at weakness; never reinforce strong resistance.
Then rebuild one from relieved or stray units.

rules.task: Decide what a group does after taking an objective
rules.when: A group has just taken an objective
do: Don't stop on it: move a short way past (design 0.1 to 0.2 x rifle).
Bring mg and light AT up at once to cover front and open flanks.
If not advancing, set all-round defense and enter cover.
Clear the whole objective.

rules.when: Force is on the defensive or holding what it took
do: Two parts forward, one back; each covers its neighbor.
Block covered approaches with troops; cover open ground with mg fire.
Depth between positions: within rifle range of each other (design 0.5 to 1.0 x rifle).
Riflemen hold fire to effective range, heavy weapons open earlier.
Prefer reverse slopes where the map offers them.

flavor.ger_reported: reverse slope, strongpoints built for all-round defense
flavor.su: uneven fire: mass suddenly on the densest attackers, then shift
flavor.jp_reported: all-round centers of resistance, outposts far forward

pitfalls: RobZ sees farther (124 m) and recognises at once, but prone in cover cuts sight to 33 m: concealment pays more, not less. Firing reveals.

rules.when: A held point has just fallen and a reserve exists
do: Go at once, whole, at the flank of the penetration.
Fire across its base to stop more entering.
Stop at the old line. Beyond it, fire only.
Enemy armor seen near and able to reach it: keep the reserve, hold a flank line, and use tac.at-screen.

flavor.ger_reported: artillery first, then immediate counterthrust by whoever is near
flavor.su: short surprise blow into flank and rear

rules.when: A group can't hold and has somewhere to go
do: Go before the enemy is within 0.5 x rifle or rifle fire is hurting you.
One part covers while the rest moves, then swap. Last out has a covered route.
Delay: spread wide, fire from maximum range, then go when he deploys.
Successive lines no farther apart than 1.0 x mg, so each covers the last.
The withdrawal is an order in both mods. Auto-move only: vanilla idle soldiers may also fall back alone, so expect leaks; RobZ idle soldiers never do (no_retreat).

scale.delay_open_fire: 1.6 to 2.4 x rifle per source, so maximum weapon range in practice

flavor.ger_reported: rear company leapfrogs through the others until dark
flavor.su: fire until he is disrupted, never wait for the assault, commander last
flavor.uk: next position organized before leaving this one

rules.when: Enemy armor is possible on a route
do: Be in place before tanks arrive. Stay hidden.
Site for flank shots; platoons cover each other's dead ground.
Hold fire inside gun range (design 0.6 x gun_medium, or vision if shorter). Others stay silent until enemy tanks turn toward the first gun.
Save AT ammunition for armor. Never chase.
Keep infantry next to the guns; don't call terrain impassable.

scale.mass: share kept together grows as guns get fewer

pitfalls: RobZ: longer gun range and near-instant recognition make surprise weaker; test the ratio.

rules.task: Combine tanks and infantry in an attack
rules.when: A group with tanks attacks
do: Default: support fires frontally, tanks go under cover to a flank.
Known AT obstacles or fortifications: infantry first, tanks fire from behind.
When tanks lead, infantry follows at once, in small groups clear of the tanks.
Assault only once AT weapons are gone; all together.
Stalled: fall back to a rally point and retry.

flavor.ger_reported: tanks bound cover to cover; infantry rides to the line
flavor.su: tanks stay close to their infantry; carry riflemen if short of transport

pitfalls: Bailed crews aren't re-crewed in stock (AI-13).

rules.task: Set a tank's target priority and when it halts
rules.when: A tank has targets, or is about to fire on the move
do: Order: enemy tanks that can hurt it, AT guns, harmless armor, troops.
Against an AT gun: some fire from cover, others close from a flank.
Halt briefly, in cover, to shoot; beyond short range don't fire on the move for effect.
Stay within support of another tank.
pitfalls: One target list per vehicle (AI-06). Hatch gunners (AI-20) count separately.

rules.when: Mortars are available and ammunition is finite
do: Fire at located guns or men, clearly stopping the advance, and on counterattacks.
Never search woods, crests, big building groups or unknown areas.
Keep them under central control, near the front.
Save some for reserves that exploit without a fire plan.

flavor.su: lift to depth at the assault, to cut infantry from tanks
flavor.uk: stay forward, fire at once; keep some for reserves

pitfalls: Stock bots have no artillery fire missions (AI-11).

rules.when: A group must cross ground an enemy weapon watches, or an unseen weapon fires
do: Located target in range: HE. Unlocated or out of range: smoke on it or its field of view.
Smoke the enemy weapon, never a curtain in front of own units.
Start just before the move, keep it up until cover: rounds = (gap / speed) / profile smoke life (vanilla about 60 s, RobZ grenade about 90 s).
Skip if it blinds own overwatch or a neighbour's lane. Wind moves no smoke in game, so doctrine wind rules drop out.
Enemy smoke: laid weapons keep firing on approaches; reserve moves up.

flavor.uk: smoke as artificial defilade against flank fire
flavor.su: plan for enemy smoke

pitfalls: No bot artillery missions (AI-11).
Wind does not move smoke (VIS-16).
Smoke life is fixed per mod: read the profile.

rules.when: Enemy weapons unknown, or the enemy shows a lone or easy target
do: A cheap element shows itself or fires; hidden killers are laid where a reply would come from and hit it at once.
Only units named for it engage scouts and lone vehicles; AT guns hold to the set range.
Feint on a second axis; if it finds weakness it becomes the main effort.
Withdrawing: a few weapons keep firing to mimic the position.
Ambush in close ground or defiles: open close, keep a way out, never chase.

flavor.su: covering platoons fire while others leave
flavor.ger: sniper lures fire with a dummy

pitfalls: RobZ RecognizeTime 0.01 weakens ambush.
No dummy units in stock AS2.

rules.when: Defending a ridge or rise the enemy can see from his side, or under enemy artillery or long-range tank fire
do: Main position just behind the crest, out of sight of enemy units beyond close range; weapons laid on the crest line.
One or two outposts on the forward slope or crest to see and warn; they fall back on contact.
Most of the force held back as a counterattack group aimed at the crest.
If the crest is lost, counterattack it at once: whoever holds it sees the whole position.
Woods count as a reverse slope; sit back from the wood edge, not on it.

scale.team: one bot holds the crest line

flavor.ger_reported: second ridge fires onto the first crest
flavor.su: dominated once the crest is lost

pitfalls: Needs per-map height data to find crests.
Long-range mods (RobZ) make the forward slope even less tenable.

rules.when: Own force is weaker or holding, and the enemy must pass through close ground (woods, town, defile, hedges)
do: Two or more parties on both sides of the route, staggered so their fire does not cross into each other.
Hold fire until the main body is in close range; let the scouts through.
One unit opens the ambush, all fire at once; first targets are leaders, AT crews and vehicles stopped by mines.
Against tanks: mine or block the lead and rear vehicles first.
Strike, then leave by a planned covered route before the enemy can reply in strength; never chase.

scale.team: ambush on the enemy's likely path to an objective

flavor.su: fire then bayonet, take prisoners

pitfalls: RobZ RecognizeTime 0.01 makes spotting near instant, so ambush works best in dense cover.
Hold fire must be set on units, or they open on the scouts.

rules.when: Attack: a route the enemy does not watch exists past his line. Defense: enemy infantry appears behind or between posts
do: Attack: send a small, well-armed group (SMG, MG, light mortar) along the unwatched route while the main attack holds the front.
Its targets are the enemy's rear: heavy weapons, AT guns, crews, and the line the main attack must cross.
Defense: every post can fire all round; do not pull posts back when infiltrators appear.
Use the reserve to hunt the infiltrators, pivoting on the posts.

flavor.su: SMG gunners in the enemy's formation
flavor.jp_reported: an LMG in the rear unsettles

pitfalls: Needs knowledge of what the enemy can see: use own vision map, not omniscience.

rules.when: Enemy tanks within close range of own infantry with grenades, charges, AT rifles or flame
do: Most infantry fire on the infantry with or behind the tanks; separated tanks are far easier to kill.
Named hunter teams, about one per platoon, close in from the rear or flank where the tank cannot see.
Strike the lead tank first; tanks stopped by mines, obstacles or town streets are first targets.
Do not send hunters across open ground in the tank's view.

flavor.su: AT rifles on dug-in tanks in towns

pitfalls: Grenade and charge reach are per mod; read the profile.
Bailed crews are not re-crewed (AI-13).

rules.when: A bunker, pillbox, emplaced gun or fortified building blocks the advance
do: Find it: embrasures, and where it can flank the approach.
Guns, tanks or MGs fire on the embrasures from a flank; smoke blinds the rest.
Engineers clear wire or mines; the assault party closes from the side the embrasures don't cover, with flame or charges.
Other units bypass it and watch its exits; once it is silent, the attack continues at once.

flavor.su: assault group with sappers and guns

pitfalls: Flame reach and pillbox armour are per mod.
No bot artillery fire missions (AI-11).

rules.task: Use assault guns and tank destroyers
rules.when: Force has assault guns or tank destroyers
do: Assault guns go with the infantry of the main effort, firing HE on the points that hold it up.
Tank destroyers wait in overwatch for tanks, away from close enemy infantry, with their own infantry or MG cover.
Either can fire on bunkers once enemy AT is suppressed.
pitfalls: Role tags differ per mod; unknown vehicles use the universal core.

rules.when: Enemy units are falling back, or his force ratio drops sharply in a sector
do: Go at once with the nearest fast units; don't wait for neighbours.
Press on a broad front against his flanks; send groups by the shortest routes to cut his retreat.
Bring MGs, mortars and guns forward so he can't re-form.
Bypass strongpoints and rearguards; stop at a set limit (his next prepared line or own support range) and consolidate.

flavor.su: commanders at the head; only a senior commander halts it

pitfalls: Chasing into an untouched AT screen is the usual loss: stop at the limit.
Retreat settings only govern idle units on AI auto-move; pursuit is an order.

rules.when: Own or enemy snipers present, or a hidden weapon is firing
do: Own sniper: forward or on a flank, apart from the platoon; first targets are MG crews, AT crews, officers and spotters.
Move after firing or after a miss; mark targets for MGs and mortars.
Against enemy snipers: watch roofs, towers and steeples; clear them early.
Find a hidden enemy with searching fire or a cheap unit moving to tempt a shot, then answer with HE.

flavor.su: hidden fire points first

pitfalls: Morale follows health in stock AS2, so officer kills matter less than in doctrine.

rules.when: Any defense with machine guns
do: Site MGs on the flanks of the position, firing across the front, not straight ahead.
Neighbouring MGs' fields cross; check each flank is covered.
Heavy MGs take the long fixed lines; light MGs fill the gaps near posts.

flavor.uk: no gaps especially at the flanks
flavor.ger_reported: strongpoints with up to six MGs

pitfalls: MG range is per mod; read the profile.

rules.task: Move a group to the fight
rules.when: A group is moving and contact is not yet made
do: Use covered routes first, in column while cover lasts.
Open ground: spread groups to about 1.5 x rifle apart (design).
Stop at terrain bounds; the next group moves only once this bound is secure.
Air or tank warning: leave the road for the nearest cover, disperse.

flavor.su: column as long as cover allows; SMG teams infiltrate ahead
flavor.jp_reported: advance guard seizes key ground first
flavor.ger_reported: infantry guide assault guns round mines

pitfalls: Doctrine yard values are wartime marches. Use the order of actions, not the distance.

rules.when: Enemy positions are unknown or an axis is being chosen
do: Send at least two elements together, never one alone.
One covers while the other moves up, then dashes back to draw fire and reveal guns.
Superior force: don't fight; bypass, mark it, and keep one element watching.
Feed what is found to axis choice and to the AT and mortar target lists.
Fight only to break through or to avoid destruction.

flavor.su: observation first; ambush only when it must
flavor.us: section per route; hold enemy flanks after contact

pitfalls: RobZ recognition is near-instant, so a scout is seen as fast as it sees.

rules.when: Objective is a built-up area
do: Bypass with leading groups if possible; a following group clears.
Fire element suppresses street-facing windows; assault elements enter from the rear.
Assault sections alternate clearing and covering; fire element moves up in bounds.
Don't encircle: leave one retreat line and cover it with a fire element or tanks.
Defending: hold inside the built-up area, not on its edge.

flavor.uk: fire section, two clearing sections, ambush party on the way out
flavor.ger_reported: main line inside the town, irregular for flank fire
flavor.su: reinforced platoon strongpoint, stocked to last

pitfalls: Almost all of this comes from one UK manual, read only on the lighter pass.
Top-down entry is only an ideal, and may not be expressible in the game.

rules.when: Route or objective lies in woods
do: Cross open ground to the near edge under smoke or concealment if possible.
Halt briefly inside the edge, not on it, to restore contact.
Keep the reserve within about 1 x rifle of the lead.
Stop short of the far edge, then leave in one rush if shelled, or filter out if under small-arms fire.
Soviet habit worth copying: bypass a strong woodland point and let followers kill it.

flavor.su: clearing to clearing, trail to trail
flavor.ger_reported: close up, then all rush out at once

pitfalls: Doctrine's 300 to 500 yards is too long for most maps, hence the ratio.

rules.when: Mission or weather shortens vision
do: Keep groups in column and deploy only close to the objective.
No envelopment: one direct assault on a point already scouted.
Narrow each weapon's sector and raise density on the line.
A group that stops loses its order: set all-round defense where it stands.
Patrol the gaps between held points.

flavor.ger: reconnoiter the night before; go for flank or rear
flavor.jp_reported: thin line left on the front by night to mask withdrawal

pitfalls: German 'go for flank or rear' and US 'straight ahead' disagree. Default to straight ahead; use the German form only as flavor.

rules.when: A river, bridge or ford lies on the axis
do: Cover the far bank with fire before anything crosses.
Cross at more than one point when the map allows.
Infantry first, abreast; heavy weapons and vehicles after the far bank holds.
Rally on the first prominent feature; don't stop on the bank.
Lead elements take an undefended crossing at once rather than waiting.

flavor.su: fords and bridges first, ice in winter

pitfalls: Boat doctrine doesn't apply. Only the choke logic carries over.

rules.when: A sniper unit is available
do: Target order: gun and mortar crews, MG crews, commanders, then enemy snipers.
Site offset from the squad, at sector limits or open flanks.
Fire a few rounds, then change position.
Attack: stay just behind the firing line, with the security element.

flavor.ger: observer pair, 3 to 6 rounds per position

pitfalls: Lighter-pass reads only. Crew removal is how it fits the game, not a source claim of value.

rules.task: Use heavy guns or fire support
rules.when: Heavy guns or fire support are available
do: Targets, in order: AT guns, observation posts, enemy guns, front-line positions.
Keep impact a clear margin from own troops; lift when the assault closes.
Don't spend it on what tanks or mortars reach faster, or on clearing mines.
Sudden short fire, then move; no long preparation.

flavor.ger_reported: rockets and mortars instead of massed guns
flavor.su: guns forward in direct fire with storm groups

pitfalls: Stock bots have no artillery fire missions (AI-11).

rules.task: Place mines, wire or tank traps
rules.when: Defending with engineers or a build option
do: Put obstacles only where a weapon covers them.
Keep them outside grenade range of own positions.
Use them to turn tanks into AT fire, not as a wall.
Guard any working party.

flavor.su: at least 50 m from trenches

pitfalls: Weakest evidence in the pack; mostly lighter-pass reads.

rules.when: Map is winter, with slow off-road movement
do: Value villages and woods more when choosing axes and held points.
Expect slow off-road flanks; plan shorter maneuvers.
Check tank routes before committing them.

flavor.su: ski raids into the rear where the mod has ski troops

pitfalls: Single nation, lighter-pass read only. Shelter has no game effect, so only the roads and terrain carry over.

personas.title: Competent commander, no nation
personas.lobby_note: Fallback for unknown armies; plays the core rules only.

personas.title: US rifle battalion, 1944

traits.do: Lead with fire: mortars and MGs on the objective before any rifle squad moves.
Put the main line on the reverse slope when the forward slope is under observed fire.
Counter infiltration with posts that hold alone and a reserve that strikes hard.
Prefer waiting for fire support over a bare assault.

personas.lobby_note: Methodical; strong with support weapons, slow without them.

traits.do: Screen every crossing of open ground; move once the smoke is thick.
Consolidate at once on each objective before the next bound.
Stick to the fire plan's objectives; exploit only inside them.

personas.title: German battle group, 1944 (reported doctrine)

traits.do: Counterattack a lost position at once, close behind the fire, at the flank of the break-in.
Build strongpoints round MGs, heavy mortars and an SP gun, firing all round.
One narrow main effort with the heavy weapons massed behind it.

personas.lobby_note: Aggressive counterattacks; dangerous to push into. German doctrine here is reported by other nations.

personas.title: Soviet rifle regiment, summer 1941

traits.do: Attack straight down the ordered axis; do not shift to a found gap.
Hold or counterattack; withdraw only on a direct order from the top.
Feed the reserve into a stalled attack rather than holding it back.

personas.lobby_note: Larp lore, not doctrine: frontal and costly on purpose. Its own manuals asked for initiative; this persona plays the 1941 reputation.

personas.title: Soviet Guards rifle division, 1944

traits.do: Mass most forces and fire on the main blow where ground gives cover and observation.
On finding a gap, leaders push through on their own, even off direction.
Fix a town frontally with part; send the main blow round to its rear.

personas.lobby_note: Heavy, fast main blow and bold exploitation.

personas.title: Japanese infantry, 1942 (reported doctrine)

traits.do: Fake strength in front with noise and automatic fire while the main force goes round a flank.
Under a holding attack, send LMG and grenade patrols round the flanks into the rear.
Prefer attacks when vision is short.
When a group is losing, charge instead of falling back.

personas.lobby_note: Flanking and night attacks; at high fidelity it charges when losing. All doctrine here is reported by the US and UK.

personas.title: Finnish battalion, winter 1939-40

traits.do: Use snipers heavily from hides, as reported of Finnish practice.
Ambush road-bound columns from the woods.
Cut a stalled column into pockets and destroy them one by one.

personas.lobby_note: Needs a mod with a Finnish army or a winter map; maps to no stock army. Finnish practice here is reported.

personas.title: What-if: modern ideas on a WW2 force
personas.lobby_note: Not period play: re-plans on events, commits the reserve behind success. For comparison against period personas.

missions.title: Hedgerow fields, Normandy 1944
missions.win: Attacker takes three field flags in turn before time runs out.
missions.teaches: Tanks and infantry clear one field at a time, each covering the other.

missions.title: Hold the reverse slope
missions.win: Defender holds the crest-line flag to the end.
missions.teaches: Defend behind the crest and counterattack troops that come over it.

missions.title: Forest road in winter
missions.win: The column reaches the far road flag, or the defender cuts it into two or more pieces.
missions.teaches: A road-bound force in forest is ambushed in pieces.

missions.title: Encircle the town, 1944
missions.win: The attacker takes the road flag behind the town and the town centre.
missions.teaches: Fix the town frontally and send the main blow round it.

missions.title: Noise in front, attack on the flank, 1942
missions.win: The attacker takes the rear flag.
missions.teaches: Don't swing the whole defence to face the noise; keep a reserve for the flank.

missions.title: Break a bunker line
missions.win: The attacker destroys or takes two of three bunkers.
missions.teaches: Fire on the embrasures and smoke the bunker's neighbours while engineers close in.

missions.title: Force a river line
missions.win: The attacker holds a far-bank flag for the last third of the match.
missions.teaches: Cross wide on a screened front and dig in on the far bank before the counterattack.

missions.title: Retake the village at dawn
missions.win: The defender has just taken the village. The attacker must retake it, and the defender must consolidate in time.
missions.teaches: Consolidate quickly, and counterattack before the enemy has.

missions.title: Night attack on a perimeter
missions.win: The attacker takes the command-post flag.
missions.teaches: Short vision favours whoever is closest and quietest. MGs on fixed lines hold the perimeter.

missions.title: Pursue a withdrawing enemy
missions.win: The defender gets half its force past the crossroads flag.
missions.teaches: Push a fast group past the rearguard. The withdrawal is always ordered, not left to auto-move.

modern.title: Decision cycle (OODA)
modern.idea: Shorten your own loop; lengthen the enemy's with surprise, deception and multiple threats.
modern.game_use: Re-plan on events (contact, loss, flag change), not on a fixed timer. Two simultaneous threats cost the opposing bot more than one strong one.
modern.caution: A faster loop with bad orientation just makes mistakes quicker; keep the scouting step.

modern.title: Mission command
modern.idea: Intent survives contact; detailed plans do not.
modern.game_use: Team or bot level issues an objective plus purpose (seize, fix, screen); the group layer chooses its path and may exploit a gap inside that purpose.
modern.caution: Needs a shared rule for when a group may abandon its task; otherwise groups drift.

modern.title: Maneuver warfare
modern.idea: Win by dislocation and collapse, not by attrition of every unit.
modern.game_use: Score sectors by enemy density; route the main effort at low-density sectors toward flags or guns behind the line.
modern.caution: Small AS2 maps often have no real gap; fall back to fix-and-flank.

modern.title: Recon-pull and surfaces and gaps
modern.idea: Commit reserves where things are going well, not where they are failing.
modern.game_use: Keep the reserve uncommitted until scout reports or early progress pick an axis; send it after success, not to rescue a stalled attack.
modern.caution: Needs live scouting; without it this is a guess.

modern.title: Movement techniques
modern.idea: Movement speed is traded for security as contact gets closer.
modern.game_use: Three movement modes keyed to distance from last known enemy (in profile vision ratios): column move, one-up-one-watching, alternate bounds.
modern.caution: Bounding is slow; on tight timers use it only inside likely-contact range.

modern.title: Suppression as an effect
modern.idea: Suppression is a time window, not a damage total.
modern.game_use: Tie the assault group's go signal to support fire actually landing; if the game has no suppression model, use smoke and fire volume as the proxy.
modern.caution: Stock AS2 morale follows health, so the effect is weaker than doctrine assumes.

modern.title: Defeat mechanisms
modern.idea: Choose the mechanism before choosing the units.
modern.game_use: Plan label for a bot: destroy (trade), dislocate (flank past), isolate (cut a sector off and take its flags).
modern.caution: Labels only help if they change buys and routes.

modern.title: Tempo and culmination
modern.idea: Know when to switch from attack to defense.
modern.game_use: Track own strength against the start of the push; under a threshold, switch the group to consolidate and dig in on the gained flag.
modern.caution: Threshold is a design value, not a source value.

modern.title: Find, fix, finish
modern.idea: A clean sequence for any echelon's attack.
modern.game_use: Group state machine: scout until contact, support group fixes, assault group finishes, reserve exploits.
modern.caution: Fixing needs a real base of fire; with too few MGs, use mortar or tank fire.

modern.title: Combined arms dilemma
modern.idea: Pose a dilemma, not a single threat.
modern.game_use: Attack groups pair tanks with infantry and indirect fire; count it as a pitfall when a group attacks with one arm only.
modern.caution: Coordination is the hard part; a pairing that moves at different speeds breaks apart.
